findings.title: Caller's ?field= list is applied to the internal error-ID lookup: 500 on unknown field, silent drop of error context
findings.body:
The new lookup calls `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))`. `process_raw_response` runs `generate_restricted_fieldset` (src/sentry/replays/post_process.py:101-110), which, when `fields` is non-empty, builds `{field: item[field] for field in fields}`. Two failures follow:

1. `?field=<any name not in the normalized row>` raises KeyError inside the request, which becomes a 500.
2. `?field=id` (or any list without `error_ids`) drops `error_ids` from the row, so `response[0].get("error_ids", [])` at line 84 returns [] and the error context disappears without any error.

The `field` parameter is not used by this endpoint for its output (it returns the paginated Seer summary), so it should not reach this lookup at all. Call `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=[])` so the lookup always sees every field.

verification.reason: The endpoint passes the caller's `field` list to `process_raw_response`, and `generate_restricted_fieldset` builds `{field: item[field] for field in fields}`. An unknown field raises KeyError (a 500), and a list without `error_ids` drops it, so line 84 silently gets [].

findings.title: Every error is repeated in every page of segments sent to Seer
findings.body: `paginate` calls `on_results` once per page (src/sentry/api/base.py:547-552), and the default page size is 100 segments (src/sentry/api/base.py:77, 493). `functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, error_events)` passes the full `error_events` list to each page. `gen_request_data` starts with `error_idx = 0` on every call, yields errors that precede a page's events, and then yields all remaining errors at lines 164-168. So each page's request contains every error in the replay, and errors are placed at the wrong position for every page after the first. For replays longer than about 100 segments, the LLM input repeats errors and misorders them, with no error signalled. Either filter `error_events` to the page's time window, or emit errors only once (for example on the first page).

verification.reason: `paginate` calls `on_results` with the current page's segments, and the partial binds the full `error_events` list. `gen_request_data` resets `error_idx` to 0 and flushes all remaining errors at the end, so every paginated request sends every error to Seer. On later pages, errors earlier than the page's events are emitted before them.

findings.title: Unknown report types now reject the whole batch with 422 (previously accepted)
findings.body: Before this change the loop did `BrowserReport(**report)`. The dataclass's `type: BrowserReportType` Literal is not checked at runtime, so any `type` string was accepted and counted. Now `type` is a `ChoiceField` limited to the eight listed values (line 40), and the first invalid report makes the handler return 422 for the entire batch before any metric is recorded (lines 109-118). Reporting API types outside the list (for example `network-error` from NEL, if this endpoint receives them) are now dropped, with only a warning log left behind. Confirm the list is exhaustive for what this endpoint receives, or count unknown types instead of rejecting them.

verification.reason: `type` is now a ChoiceField over eight values, and the first invalid report returns 422 for the whole batch before any metric is recorded. Previously the dataclass Literal was not enforced at runtime. The new test_rejects_invalid_report_type shows the rejection is deliberate, so this is a design question rather than a bug.

findings.title: drain_mailbox_parallel's 120 s processing deadline is shorter than the loop's own 180 s budget
findings.body: `drain_mailbox_parallel` now declares `processing_deadline_duration=120`. Its loop runs until `deadline = timezone.now() + BATCH_SCHEDULE_OFFSET` (line 294), and `BATCH_SCHEDULE_OFFSET = timedelta(minutes=BACKOFF_INTERVAL)` (line 44) with `BACKOFF_INTERVAL = 3` (src/sentry/hybridcloud/models/webhookpayload.py:18), so the loop is designed to run for 180 s. The broker can abort the task at 120 s, mid-batch. If aborted tasks are re-run, in-flight webhooks can be delivered again. Set the deadline above the loop budget plus one batch, or shorten the loop budget. I did not verify the broker's abort-and-retry behaviour.
findings.originReason: In the base the task had no explicit deadline and used the 10 s default, which was already far below the 180 s loop budget.

verification.reason: The loop runs until now + BATCH_SCHEDULE_OFFSET (3 minutes = 180 s), but the task's processing deadline is 120 s, so the worker can be killed mid-batch. Before this change the task fell back to DEFAULT_PROCESSING_DEADLINE = 10 s, so the mismatch already existed and this diff narrows it.

findings.title: 30 s deadline for schedule_webhook_delivery: is it enough at the worst case?
findings.body: The scheduler iterates up to `BATCH_SIZE = 1000` mailboxes (line 137), and for each one runs a filter, an UPDATE and a `.delay()` (lines 140-152). A 30 s processing deadline may be exceeded at full batch size, in which case the broker aborts the scheduler mid-loop. Was 30 s measured against a realistic backlog?

verification.reason: The deadline went from the 10 s default to 30 s, which loosens the limit. Whether 30 s covers a full 1000-mailbox batch depends on runtime numbers that the code does not show.

findings.title: 60 s deadline on a task that performs up to 100 external IdP refreshes
findings.body: `check_auth_identities` processes `chunk_size` identities (default 100 at line 36), each with `provider.refresh_identity` (line 128), which calls an external identity provider with no per-call bound visible in this task. What was the previous effective deadline, and was 60 s measured against a full chunk?

verification.reason: The previous effective deadline was the 10 s default (auth_control_tasks sets none), so 60 s loosens the limit. Whether 60 s is enough for 100 IdP refreshes cannot be decided from the code.

findings.title: autofix_automation_tuning default flips from 'low' to 'off' for every unset project

The PR body is "Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System" and does not mention this. Is the flip intended, and does it need a release note or a data migration for existing projects?

verification.reason: Both the project option default and DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT change from 'low' to 'off'. `_is_issue_fixable` returns False for 'off', so autofix stops for every project that never stored the option.

The real `tableResults[i]` and `fields` are not passed, so the table shows no columns and no rows. The flag is not registered in src/sentry/features (no match for `use-table-widget-visualization`), so no one sees this today. Either pass the real data and columns, or keep the existing `StyledSimpleTableChart` path until the wiring exists.

verification.reason: Behind the flag, TableWidgetVisualization gets hardcoded empty columns and data, so the real results are never shown. The flag name appears only in chart.tsx and is not registered, so this looks like unfinished scaffolding that no user sees today.

findings.title: Issue title is interpolated unescaped into markdown link text
findings.body: The title, which comes from customer event data, is now placed inside `[**{title}**]({url})` (line 143, used at lines 600-606). Characters such as `]`, `(`, `*` or a newline can close the link text early and add a link or break the list. The old template also interpolated the title unescaped, so this is not new in kind, but the link structure makes it easier to break. Consider escaping markdown-significant characters in the title before formatting.

verification.reason: The issue title is truncated but not escaped before it is placed inside `[**{title}**]({url})`, so markdown characters in a title can break the link. The old template also interpolated the title unescaped.

findings.title: Header layout lost align-items:center and gap when FlexBox was replaced by Flex
findings.body: The removed Container = styled(FlexBox) set display:flex, align-items:center and gap: space(1). It is replaced by <Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">. Flex (static/app/components/core/layout/flex.tsx:18-26) emits align-items and gap only when those props are passed, so the row now uses align-items: normal (stretch) and no gap. The tabs and vitals no longer center vertically and lose their minimum spacing. The second group in Placeholder (line 27) had the same FlexBox centering and gap before. Pass align="center" gap={space(1)} to both Flex containers.

verification.reason: Flex emits align-items and gap only from props. The main container passes only `justify`, and the second Placeholder group passes nothing, so both lose the `align-items: center` and the `gap` that FlexBox used to set.

findings.title: Attribute-keys query key omits the organization
findings.body: The query key is ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions], and queryOptions has no organization. The request at static/app/views/explore/hooks/useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:78 uses organization.slug. The old key was the request path, which contained the org slug. With 'All projects' the project list is empty in both orgs, so two organizations in one session produce the same key. The cache then serves org A's attribute names to org B, and the usePrevious ref keeps them on screen during the refetch. Add organization.slug to the key.

verification.reason: The queryKey is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, and `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` contains no org, while the fetch URL uses organization.slug. Two orgs with the same project/date selection therefore share one cache entry.

findings.title: Dropping retry:false and mapping isLoading to isFetching changes loading and error behavior
findings.body: The old useApiQuery call passed retry:false, staleTime:0 and refetchOnWindowFocus:false. The new useQuery call drops retry:false. The app QueryClient config (static/app/utils/queryClient.tsx:19-25) overrides only the refetch options, so react-query's default retry applies. A failing request therefore stays in the fetching state through its retries before error is set. Separately, isLoading is now isFetching (line 61) rather than pending-and-fetching, so cached data reports loading during every background refetch on mount. Restore retry:false, and keep isLoading pending-only if its consumers expect that.

verification.reason: The new `useQuery` call drops `retry: false`, and the global config overrides only the refetch options, so react-query's default retries apply. `isLoading` is now `isFetching`, so it is also true during background refetches.

findings.title: Truthiness check treats falsy custom cell values as 'no custom renderer'
findings.body: if (cell) (line 70, and line 31 for headers) falls back to the default renderer for any falsy return, including 0, '' and false. The documented contract (tableWidgetVisualization.tsx:41-43 and 52-54, and the story at tableWidgetVisualization.stories.tsx:111-114) says only undefined falls back. A custom renderer that returns 0 for a zero-count cell is silently replaced by the default value. Use cell !== undefined in both places. No caller in this snapshot returns a falsy value, so this is latent.

verification.reason: `if (cell)` falls back to the default renderer for any falsy return, such as 0 or ''. The documented contract returns `React.ReactNode | undefined`, which implies only undefined should fall back. This is latent.

findings.title: `Flex.Item grow={1}` is not the `flex: 1` it replaces
findings.body: The removed `FlexContainer` set `flex: 1` (flex 1 1 0%). `Flex.Item grow={1}` emits only flex-grow:1, flex-shrink:1 and flex-basis:auto (static/app/components/core/layout/flex.tsx:41-45). With basis auto, the description's max-content width now takes part in the space split, so a long integration description can squeeze the Metadata column (author and resource links, integrationLayout.tsx:362-371, which has margin-right 100px). `<Flex.Item flex={1}>` emits `flex: 1` (flex.tsx:36-40) and keeps the old rule. I did not render the page: the basis difference follows from the CSS, but how much it shows depends on content.

verification.reason: `Flex.Item grow={1}` emits flex-grow 1, flex-shrink 1 and flex-basis auto, while the removed rule was `flex: 1` (basis 0%). `flex={1}` would keep the old rule. How visible the difference is depends on content.

findings.title: "Project not found" can show while projects are still loading
findings.body: The new branch treats `project === undefined` as not found. `useProjectFromId` returns only what is in the projects store (static/app/utils/useProjectFromId.tsx:9-12). `useProjects` exposes `store.projects`, which is empty until the store loads (static/app/utils/useProjects.tsx:159-163, 303-305), plus a `fetching` and `initiallyLoaded` state (lines 312-313) that this branch does not read. If the AI tab can render before the store has loaded, the user sees a wrong error until the store fills in, and then it self-corrects. Question for the author: does the replay detail page guarantee the projects store is loaded before the AI tab renders? If not, gate the error on the loading state.

verification.reason: The new branch treats a missing project as not found without checking whether the projects store has loaded. Whether the store is always loaded before this tab renders cannot be decided from the files read.

findings.title: PUT owner tests cover only the success paths
findings.body: The new PUT tests (test_update_owner_to_user, test_update_owner_to_team, test_update_clear_owner) cover only successful owner changes. Two cases are not exercised on PUT. summary:
**Batch 1 of 4.** Nothing in this part is a blocker. Five fix-level findings: the replay summary's internal error lookup passes the caller's ?field= list through (500 on unknown names, silent drop of error context); error events are repeated in every page of Seer input; browser-report validation now rejects whole batches on unknown types; drain_mailbox_parallel's 120 s processing deadline is shorter than its 180 s loop budget; and the autofix default flips to 'off' for every unset project, which the PR description does not mention. The PR body ("Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System") does not describe most of this diff (grouping, webhooks, autofix, devservices, feedback prompt, dashboards, grouping info). The dashboard table branch is dead today because its flag is not registered. Frontend files were reviewed from their diff hunks plus targeted searches, not read line by line; the Python files with findings were read in full.

**Batch 2 of 4.** Thirty-two files reviewed. Four findings are confirmed: the span attribute list hides its system attributes only while a search is typed (fix); the trace header lost its center alignment and gap in the FlexBox-to-Flex swap (fix); the attribute-keys query key omits the organization, so cached keys can cross orgs (fix, medium confidence); and the keys hook's dropped retry:false and isLoading-to-isFetching change loading and error behavior (consider). One latent consider covers the truthiness check in the custom cell renderers. The Visualize yAxes-to-yAxis migration has no stale callers in static/app: queryTokens and seerSearch use their own shapes, and exploreParams reads BaseVisualize. I did not report the traceWaterfall height change because I did not read that file in full. The feedback-summary and dashboard-table contracts stay open, pending files outside this part.

**Batch 3 of 4.** Reviewed all 27 files in this part. Four findings: the Flex.Item swap in integrationLayout.tsx is not equivalent to the `flex: 1` it replaces (fix); the browser-reporting test changes drop the only coverage of the application/reports+json media type (fix); the AI tab's new "Project not found" branch ignores the projects store's loading state (consider, phrased as a question about whether the page guarantees the store is loaded); and one spec's title says bar charts while it asserts LINE (consider). The other refactors (sample-rate row, audit log, CODEOWNERS table, OAuth details, upload token) keep the same CSS. The Visualize constructor, toJSON and hook-signature spec updates match the source. The PR-comment, parameterization, autofix default and migration-test changes match the source. I did not run any tests. Two of the table-widget spec's formatted strings are unverified (see the open contract). Some specs were checked by diff and by pattern search rather than full reads: toolbar/index.spec.tsx past line 70, aggregateColumnEditorModal.spec.tsx past line 70, test_project_details.py (the changed hunk only), and test_delete_replays_bulk.py (lines 50-130).

**Batch 4 of 4.** Reviewed the five test files in part 4 of 4 (replay summarize-breadcrumbs, detector details and index owner tests, delayed-workflow query tests, and events-stats ourlogs/spans tests). No blocking or fix-level defects. Checked against the source: the replay error title reaches nodestore with the exception value via materialize_metadata and compute_title, so the 'division by zero' assertion holds. The owner tests match the validator, ActorField, and serializer behaviour. The delayed-workflow helper call matches production. Three 'consider' findings concern test quality: a duplicated store_replays helper, missing PUT negative and omit-owner tests, and weak negative assertions. One contract (ourlogs topEvents) stays open because its endpoint and snuba code are outside this part.

notices: Contract "Table widget renders TableWidgetVisualization behind a feature flag": evidence not verified: src/sentry/features/temporary.py is not path:line.

entries.title: Caller's ?field= list is applied to the internal error-ID lookup: 500 on unknown field, silent drop of error context
entries.reason: The endpoint passes the caller's `field` list to `process_raw_response`, and `generate_restricted_fieldset` builds `{field: item[field] for field in fields}`. An unknown field raises KeyError (a 500), and a list without `error_ids` drops it, so line 84 silently gets [].

entries.title: Every error is repeated in every page of segments sent to Seer
entries.reason: `paginate` calls `on_results` with the current page's segments, and the partial binds the full `error_events` list. `gen_request_data` resets `error_idx` to 0 and flushes all remaining errors at the end, so every paginated request sends every error to Seer. On later pages, errors earlier than the page's events are emitted before them.

entries.title: Unknown report types now reject the whole batch with 422 (previously accepted)
entries.reason: `type` is now a ChoiceField over eight values, and the first invalid report returns 422 for the whole batch before any metric is recorded. Previously the dataclass Literal was not enforced at runtime. The new test_rejects_invalid_report_type shows the rejection is deliberate, so this is a design question rather than a bug.

entries.title: drain_mailbox_parallel's 120 s processing deadline is shorter than the loop's own 180 s budget
entries.originReason: In the base the task had no explicit deadline and used the 10 s default, which was already far below the 180 s loop budget.
entries.reason: The loop runs until now + BATCH_SCHEDULE_OFFSET (3 minutes = 180 s), but the task's processing deadline is 120 s, so the worker can be killed mid-batch. Before this change the task fell back to DEFAULT_PROCESSING_DEADLINE = 10 s, so the mismatch already existed and this diff narrows it.

entries.title: 30 s deadline for schedule_webhook_delivery: is it enough at the worst case?
entries.reason: The deadline went from the 10 s default to 30 s, which loosens the limit. Whether 30 s covers a full 1000-mailbox batch depends on runtime numbers that the code does not show.

entries.title: 60 s deadline on a task that performs up to 100 external IdP refreshes
entries.reason: The previous effective deadline was the 10 s default (auth_control_tasks sets none), so 60 s loosens the limit. Whether 60 s is enough for 100 IdP refreshes cannot be decided from the code.

entries.title: autofix_automation_tuning default flips from 'low' to 'off' for every unset project
entries.reason: Both the project option default and DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT change from 'low' to 'off'. `_is_issue_fixable` returns False for 'off', so autofix stops for every project that never stored the option.

entries.title: Behind the flag, every table widget renders an empty table and ignores the query results
entries.reason: Behind the flag, TableWidgetVisualization gets hardcoded empty columns and data, so the real results are never shown. The flag name appears only in chart.tsx and is not registered, so this looks like unfinished scaffolding that no user sees today.

entries.title: Dead _handle_regex_match left behind in parametrize_w_experiments
entries.reason: After the regex-experiment branch was removed, the nested `_handle_regex_match` in `parametrize_w_experiments` is no longer referenced. The loop only passes `_incr_counter`.

entries.title: format_comment_subtitle has no callers after this change
entries.reason: A grep across all .py files finds `format_comment_subtitle` only at its definitions. The GitHub call site now uses `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`.

entries.title: format_comment_subtitle has no callers after this change
entries.reason: `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.format_comment_subtitle` has no callers anywhere in the .py tree after the template change.

entries.title: PR comment drops the culprit line and puts a blank line between every item
entries.reason: The culprit subtitle is gone, and the trailing \n joined with "\n" puts a blank line between items. The updated GitHub and GitLab PR-comment tests expect exactly this output, so the change looks intentional.

entries.title: Issue title is interpolated unescaped into markdown link text
entries.reason: The issue title is truncated but not escaped before it is placed inside `[**{title}**]({url})`, so markdown characters in a title can break the link. The old template also interpolated the title unescaped.

entries.title: DB query injection vulnerability now has ignore_limit=5 (noise suppression)
entries.reason: The diff adds `noise_config = NoiseConfig(ignore_limit=5)` to DBQueryInjectionVulnerabilityGroupType. `should_create_group` creates a group only once times_seen reaches ignore_limit.

entries.title: The 'Type' row with its explanation is removed for every grouping variant
entries.reason: The diff removes the 'Type' row and its QuestionTooltip from the component, custom-fingerprint, built-in-fingerprint, salted and performance branches.

entries.title: Assemble analytics fires before the feature gate
entries.reason: `analytics.record` runs at line 81, before the `features.has` gate at line 88, so organizations without the flag are counted even though they get a 404.

entries.title: New feedback summary component and hook ship without spec files
entries.reason: CLAUDE.md requires colocated .spec.tsx tests. A glob finds only feedbackSummary.tsx and useFeedbackSummary.tsx, with no spec files.

entries.title: Hidden attributes are only filtered while a search is typed
entries.reason: With an empty search the memo returns `sorted` at line 62 before the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter, so the hidden attributes show unless the user types a query.

entries.title: Header layout lost align-items:center and gap when FlexBox was replaced by Flex
entries.reason: Flex emits align-items and gap only from props. The main container passes only `justify`, and the second Placeholder group passes nothing, so both lose the `align-items: center` and the `gap` that FlexBox used to set.

entries.title: Attribute-keys query key omits the organization
entries.reason: The queryKey is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, and `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` contains no org, while the fetch URL uses organization.slug. Two orgs with the same project/date selection therefore share one cache entry.

entries.title: Dropping retry:false and mapping isLoading to isFetching changes loading and error behavior
entries.reason: The new `useQuery` call drops `retry: false`, and the global config overrides only the refetch options, so react-query's default retries apply. `isLoading` is now `isFetching`, so it is also true during background refetches.

entries.title: Truthiness check treats falsy custom cell values as 'no custom renderer'
entries.reason: `if (cell)` falls back to the default renderer for any falsy return, such as 0 or ''. The documented contract returns `React.ReactNode | undefined`, which implies only undefined should fall back. This is latent.

entries.title: `Flex.Item grow={1}` is not the `flex: 1` it replaces
entries.reason: `Flex.Item grow={1}` emits flex-grow 1, flex-shrink 1 and flex-basis auto, while the removed rule was `flex: 1` (basis 0%). `flex={1}` would keep the old rule. How visible the difference is depends on content.

entries.title: No test sends application/reports+json any more
entries.reason: No .py file outside the endpoint mentions reports+json any more. The happy-path tests now post without that content_type, and the assertion on the `browser_report_received` log was removed.

entries.title: "Project not found" can show while projects are still loading
entries.reason: The new branch treats a missing project as not found without checking whether the projects store has loaded. Whether the store is always loaded before this tab renders cannot be decided from the files read.

entries.title: Test title says bar charts but asserts LINE
entries.originReason: The base spec has the same 'defaults to bar charts' title on the LINE assertions.
entries.reason: The second `it.each` is titled 'defaults to bar charts' but asserts ChartType.LINE. The base already had the same mismatched title.

entries.title: store_replays duplicates the existing ReplaysSnubaTestCase helper
entries.reason: The local `store_replays` is identical to `ReplaysSnubaTestCase.store_replays`. Reusing it is not trivial, though: that class is a TestCase that drops tables in setUp, while this test uses TransactionTestCase.

entries.title: PUT owner tests cover only the success paths
entries.reason: The PUT test class has only success-path owner tests, with no invalid or cross-org owner test and no test that omitting owner keeps it. The `"owner" in validated_data` guard is therefore not covered.

entries.title: Negative owner tests assert only that the key 'owner' is present
entries.reason: Both negative tests assert only `"owner" in response.data`, not the specific validation message.
